accuracy.evidence: Working-memory claims checked against Cowan (2001, 'The magical number 4 in short-term memory', Behavioral and Brain Sciences): about 4 chunks for adults, so the lab's 4-slot box is the adult figure and the adult text says children hold fewer; Miller (1956) 7±2 is named as an overestimate, not used. Chunking as grouping into meaningful units matches the topic description and evidence lines (phone number 3-3-4, spellings in syllables, lists into sets). Syllable splits checked: yes-ter-day, but-ter-fly, re-mem-ber, won-der-ful. Parameterised items checked at range corners: p2 g*k 4..12, p4 c*k 4..12, m5 w*3 6..15, m9 a+b 2..5; no division items, so every answer is a whole number.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real slips children (and adults) make with this strategy: memory holds 'all 9' (step 1 prediction; 5 numbers fall out), chunks 'still too many' (step 2 prediction), saying it faster helps (CQ fast, m2), one giant chunk (CQ huge, judge() 'too big for one chunk', m6), single leftovers become extra pieces (judge() 'on its own is a whole piece', CQ uneven, m7), letter-by-letter spelling (step 4 prediction, CQ letters), meaningless splits (CQ nosense, m3), and 'chunking makes memory bigger or faster' (CQ bigger/faster, p5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagchunk is built on its own mechanism: a 4-slot memory box that fills with however many pieces the child's breaks create, with the overflow spilling out, plus a gap-marker splitter reused across numbers, syllables and hidden words, and a 3-basket list sort. flagmem (11-12) models working memory, spacing and recall; flagmnem uses first-letter sentences; neither lets the child set chunk boundaries and see the piece count change. Max 6-shingle similarity 9.1% (flag_shine.js, shared kit idioms).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child sees the problem before the fix: 9 single numbers overflow the box (5 fall out); adding breaks changes the box live from 9 pieces to 3 that fit, and judge() explains bad splits (too big, single leftovers); the shopping sort ends with '9 things, but only 3 groups to remember'; the spelling and hidden-word rows show 'N pieces to remember, not 9'. Done messages then state the strategy.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options: 'all 9' numbers fit (5 fall out), 3 chunks are 'still too many' (they fit), letter-by-letter is easier to spell (the beats give 3 pieces), and C A T D O G H E N is as easy as cat dog hen (3 words versus 9 letters).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Nine distinct slip messages in slip(): single, huge, fast, hope, letters, uneven, nosense, faster, bigger. Each names the wrong idea and the fix. The splitter steps add live feedback for chunks over 4, single leftovers, and breaks off the beats or off the words, and the shopping sort says why an item does not belong in the chosen basket.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes for the family audience: kid FK 1.6, adult FK 9.0. Kid text uses short sentences, and chunk is defined as 'a group' on first use. Letter and digit tiles are drawn at up to 24 px bold on pale tiles; basket contents 13-15 px; every label is dark ink on a pale card.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases; explanation overlap 0.3% at most). Kid paragraphs: memory limit; number chunks; list groups; spelling and meaningful chunks. Adult paragraphs: EEF strategy framing and key words; Cowan vs Miller; named mistakes; what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots after Show me on every step at 360 px Android (light), iPhone 13 (dark) and desktop (dark), plus the shopping step before sorting. Fixes from the first pass: tile text shrank to about 10 px on phones, so tiles are now drawn with their own font sized to the tile; basket text went from 11 px to 13 px and baskets sit at the bottom; the shopping grid listed each category in one column, which gave the answer away, so the items are now mixed. The young class gives 56 px buttons.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button: 'Pour the 9 numbers into my memory', 'Move the gap marker left/right', 'Put a break at the marker' / 'Remove the break at the marker', 'Put apple in the Fruit basket'. tell() updates the canvas aria-label and the narration after each action, including the gap position. walk.cjs: desktop and iPhone 13 complete all 5 tasks with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes, no console errors.
